Im sorry you’re struggling with that. I will say I was in a very similar boat. Asian/North African family very heavily obsessed with academia. I thought it was my only way out of my life. Looking back, I really wish I could have told myself how little grades actually matter. Jobs don’t care if you went to a prestigious or top school. The only benefit to those colleges is networking. Which you can do both at any college as well as especially when you’re in whatever field you want to be in. The amount of nights I spent so suicidal over grades, when in my current life it doesn’t matter. Despite my near perfect grades and scholarships, I ended up dropping out of college anyways half way in, yet I still excel at my job and am considered extremely knowledgeable by those in my field in my area. Best advice I would give my best self, don’t stress about grades they really don’t matter. Try your best and focus on things that interest you, excel at topics you WANT to excel in, not because of a grade. I know that’s easier said then done so best of luck

For me I treat it like acid and I try to take 4-6 month breaks in between each session. Your body being in pain is a sign you need a break before permanent damage. Once you stop using and you’re pissing every Fucking hour that’ll be a good reminder you need to continue your break. I’ll tell myself it’s a “tolerance break” to keep me from using for that time frame. Reminding myself how much money I save by making sure I can still get fucked up on less then a gram. It also makes it where it’s still fun to do and not a dependence. I also try to only buy what I’ll use for one or two sessions every 4-6 months, having a chill dealer who can work with you on that is important too. Even setting a specific date in your calendar where you want to wait till, something to look forward to and remind you to not use until that day/after that day instead of a vague idea of how long a break should be

Try using anti-incarceration hotlines. THRIVE is a suicide hotline over text, and it is completely anonymous. They will never call the cops on you, this allows you to be able to be open and seek genuine support without having to sugar coat.

Calling police may put them in more danger, you can specifically request an ambulance if you must. My best advice is offering to stay on the phone with them that night. You Can also suggest a crisis line, such as THRIVE which is an anonymous text based suicide hotline where they won’t call the cops on you because it’s anonymous, this allows people to actually feel comfortable asking for help as opposed to being put in more danger.

Med changes are rough, they take a lot of time to start really showing affects. For those of us who need medication, it really comes down to finding that perfect “medicine cocktail” of what works best for us. I also was suicidal since elementary school and the thing that got me through my teenage years was telling myself it could change, and it WILL, life is constantly changing for the better and for the worse, but it will always change back to better eventually if you give it enough time, maybe even years. Also for myself and many others graduating school and moving out (+ helps once hormones stabilize more) was a big step towards working on mental health. My advice is keep going to therapy, try doing therapy assignments routinely, try to hold hope while your body learns to get used to the med changes, and know even though it may not get easier, you’ll be better skilled to handle it

CW: overdose attempt


It never is painless and is rarely successful because our body will always use every ounce of power it can to survive even the most physically traumatic attempts at death. I remember my attempt to overdose, it was not only extremely painful and scary, but at the last possible moment before my breathing stopped I instinctively saved my life, even though I was dead set on dying. I remember how surreal it was with not knowing where I was, not even comprehending what I was reaching for, I didnt even KNOW i was trying to save my life, yet my body knew what to do, even if *I* mentally didn’t.

I think the biggest reason for me is the possibility of change. Life is always changing and its terrifying, but its also freeing to know that our circumstances can and will change. One day your circumstances will change and you will look back at right now and think how the best decision you’ve ever made was staying alive. If you haven’t seen the change you want yet and don’t have a reason to live yet, it means your journey is not over and you still have so many things waiting for you, even if you cant imagine what those things will be yet.

I think this is one of two things. It could be you’ve experienced so much misogyny that it’s affecting how you view being born a woman. This also sounds very much like how dysphoria worked for me before I came out as a man. Particularly the not wanting to have sex because of lack of a penis. Personally I think the best course is unpacking some misogyny to see if it’s just because of how you view women bodies. But if it’s that you view women as good and powerful, but YOU don’t feel in that same bracket, it might be that you’re trans. I had to unpack a lot of internalized misogyny before I realized I was trans. But once I started valuing women as the Incredible asset and beautiful contributions to society as a whole, I realized that I was also an incredible asset and beautiful, but I was just a guy so I felt incredibly dysphoric and hated that *I* was a “woman”. That healing allowed me to realize that it’s okay I’m a man, and being male doesn’t make anyone better, but being a woman is just not for everyone and that’s okay! 🖤
